name: @immersive-media-technologies/aftereffects-mcp-imt

tools.name: ae_project_info
tools.description: Project-level info: file path, dirty flag, all items with type/summary, active item. Start here.

tools.name: ae_comp_info
tools.description: Detailed comp info: size, fps, duration, work area, motion blur, layer summaries. Pass a comp name or item id — or an ARRAY of them to fetch several comps in one call.

nameOrId.description: Composition name (exact match) or numeric item id — or an array of either to batch several comps into one round trip. If you don't know any, call ae_project_info first.

tools.name: ae_layer_info
tools.description: Full layer info: transform, effects, masks, text, shape contents, keyframes. layerIndex accepts one index, an ARRAY of indices, or 'all' — auditing a whole comp is one call. Set includeProperties=false to skip the property tree walk.

compNameOrId.description: Composition name (exact match) or numeric item id.

layerIndex.description: 1-based layer index — or an array of indices, or 'all' for every layer in the comp, returned together in one round trip.

includeProperties.description: Include the full property tree (Transform/Effects/Masks/Text). Default true.

tools.name: ae_render_frame
tools.description: Render a single frame to PNG. Use to visually verify edits. The agent's 'eyes' — pair with mutations for a visual feedback loop. Headless and deterministic. In color-managed projects (workingSpace != None) the capture applies AE's own display transform via a transient OCIO Display Transform adjustment layer, and the PNG comes back viewer-accurate and sRGB-tagged. Where that layer cannot be used — read-only mode, an AE without the OCIO effect, or a failed capture calibration — the result falls back to a pure-math ACES conversion or to raw values with an explicit colorWarning; check colorPipeline / colorWarning on the response.

compNameOrId.description: Composition name or numeric item id.

outPath.description: Absolute path to write the PNG. Parent directory is created if missing.

useDisplayStartTime.description: If true, `time` is interpreted relative to comp.displayStartTime. Default false.

compareWith.description: Absolute path of an earlier PNG (same comp size) to compare the new frame against. Adds `compare`: changedRatio (0..1 of pixels that differ), meanAbsDiff (0..1), bbox of the change — 'did my edit change the picture, and where' without reading the image.

colorManaged.description: 'auto' (default): detect the working space and return a viewer-accurate, 8-bit sRGB-tagged PNG. 'off': raw legacy output (16-bit, untagged, working-space values — dark/wrong-looking in color-managed projects).

tools.name: ae_save_project
tools.description: Save the project. Pass `path` for Save As.

path.description: Optional absolute path to save the project to (Save As). If omitted, save to the existing path — errors if the project has never been saved.

tools.name: ae_project_export_json
tools.description: Serialize the entire project to JSON (folders, comps, layers, keyframes, effects, shapes, markers, time remap, solids, file refs). Write to `outPath` or return inline.

outPath.description: If set, write the exported JSON to this absolute path on disk. If omitted, the JSON is returned inline in the tool response (can get large).

pretty.description: Pretty-print the JSON (2-space indent). Default: true when writing to disk, false otherwise.

tools.name: ae_project_import_json
tools.description: Rebuild the project from JSON (produced by ae_project_export_json). Supports `clearFirst`, `dryRun` (validate-only), `skipValidation`.

inPath.description: Absolute path to a JSON document produced by ae_project_export_json. Mutually exclusive with `json`.

json.description: Inline JSON document (object, not string). Mutually exclusive with `inPath`.

clearFirst.description: Remove all existing items from the current project before importing. Default: false (appends).

dryRun.description: If true, validate the document and return a plan without touching AE. Useful for debugging malformed exports.

skipValidation.description: Skip Node-side schema validation. Only use if you trust the input and want to hand broken data to AE for diagnosis.

tools.name: ae_version_info
tools.description: AE version, build, capabilities (saveFrameToPng, app.effects, Socket). Call at session start to know what APIs are available.

tools.name: ae_catalog
tools.description: Discover available atomic operations for ae_do. Without args: all categories with their operation names. With a category: detailed params per operation. Only operations this server will actually execute are listed.

category.description: Filter by category. Omit to list all categories with operation counts, then drill into a specific category.

tools.name: ae_do
tools.description: Execute an atomic operation by name (from ae_catalog). Arguments are validated against the operation's declared parameters before anything reaches AE. Have more than one operation to run? Wrap them in ONE batch.run instead of several ae_do calls — read/verify steps (comp.info, layer.info, render.frame) can ride in the same batch. Every call is automatically wrapped in ONE undo group: a single Ctrl+Z (or project.undo) reverts the entire call, and a batch.run counts as one call. Never call app.beginUndoGroup/endUndoGroup in eval.run code — the wrapper already did. The exception is undo/redo itself (project.undo, command.execute id 16/2035): those run outside the group and cannot ride inside a batch.run. Response includes ambient context (active comp, selected layers, project state) at zero extra round trips. Example: ae_do({ operation: 'keyframe.add', args: { comp: 'Main', layer: 1, property: ['Transform','Position'], time: 2, value: [960,540] } })

args.description: Arguments for the operation. Validated against ae_catalog's declared params: missing required args, wrong types, and unknown keys are rejected before AE is contacted. Omit for zero-param operations.

timeoutMs.description: Per-call timeout in milliseconds (default 60000). Raise for long operations like render.start or big batch.run calls.

dryRun.description: Validate the operation and return the ExtendScript that WOULD run, without contacting After Effects. Nothing is executed and the project is not touched. Use it to preview a destructive call before committing to it.

tools.name: ae_context
tools.description: Ambient context: project state, active comp, selected layers, item list, AE.* helpers, ES3 rules, and the undo contract (every call = one auto undo group). Call at session start; then rely on ae_do response context.

tools.name: ae_dialogs
tools.description: List the modal dialogs After Effects is showing, or dismiss one by its cancel action (what Escape does: a warning is acknowledged, a 'save changes?' question is cancelled — never answered for the user). Use after a DIALOG_OPEN / TIMEOUT error, or before a step known to pop a dialog. Windows + macOS; on macOS reading the text and dismissing need Accessibility permission for the app that runs this server.

action.description: list — report open dialogs; dismiss — close the one named by `id`.

id.description: Dialog id from a previous list / DIALOG_OPEN error (required for dismiss).

tools.name: ae_object_matte_ui
tools.description: Object Matte (AE 26) on a layer through After Effects' UI — macOS only; no script can create a selection. Give lassos and points in the pixels of a frame you looked at (comp pixels of an ae_render_frame by default, or layer source pixels with space:"layer"). A LASSO takes the subjects inside the outline — AE snaps it to their silhouettes — so one lasso can take a whole group of people at once: outline them generously, heads and feet with a margin. A POINT takes the subject under it as AE segments it — often only a garment or a torso in a crowd, so use points only for a lone, clearly separated subject. mode:"subtract" removes (Option). The tool opens the layer in the Layer panel at `time` (the base frame), makes the Object Matte tool active (checked through the active-tool code — Option+W is the Roto Brush group's shortcut and cycles its members), acts with real mouse events, reads back the strokes the effect recorded (error_px = where each landed vs where it was meant to), optionally propagates by stepping the comp time (propagate_to), and then RENDERS A PREVIEW and returns it as images: top — the matte over black, bottom — the frame with the excluded parts in red, with markers: cyan boxes on gaps between kept pieces (where a hidden, lying or partly visible person is usually left out) and green/yellow rings on the `people` points you listed. A part of a person, someone behind another or lying on the ground is a subject too: add it with a lasso that overlaps the neighbouring kept matte so the pieces merge. The result is never verified by the tool: look at the images and check every person. With only preview_times (no points, lassos or propagate_to) it renders the preview without touching the UI — use it to check any frames. The Layer panel must be visible and large enough for the whole picture.

layer.description: 1-based layer index or layer name (the layer that gets the matte — the plate).

time.description: Composition time (s) of the base frame the points were picked on.

points.description: Clicks: each takes the subject under it as AE segments it (in a crowd often only a part — prefer lassos).

lassos.description: Closed outlines (≥ 3 points each, ~12–40 points following the group's contour with a margin): each takes the subjects inside it, snapped to their silhouettes.

mode.description: add (default): Shift-click / lasso adds to the matte; subtract: Option-click / Option-lasso removes.

space.description: Coordinate space of points and lassos: comp (default — pixels of an ae_render_frame of this comp) or layer (source pixels).

zoom.description: Layer panel zoom to set before acting (1 = 100 %). Default: the current zoom, lowered until the picture fits 45 % of the window width.

propagate_to.description: After the actions, step the comp time from `time` to this time frame by frame so AE propagates the matte (both directions allowed).

settle_ms.description: Pause per propagated frame (default 250 ms; raise on 4K).

preview.description: Render the preview after the actions (default true).

preview_times.description: Times (s) to preview. Default: the base frame, plus propagate_to when given. Alone (no points/lassos/propagate_to) = preview only, no UI.

preview_region.description: Comp-pixel rectangle to preview at higher detail (e.g. a group of people) instead of the whole frame.

preview_width.description: Width of each preview panel in pixels (default 1000).

preview_overlay.description: Add the bottom panel with excluded parts in red (default true; renders the frame once more with the effect switched off, then restores it).

people.description: Your checklist of the people who belong in the matte, picked on the frame `people_time` in COMP pixels: a point on each one's head, body and feet (any you can see). The preview marks each point green (inside the matte) or yellow (outside) and reports whole / partial / missing per person. Pass it on every call.

people_time.description: Frame (s) the people points were picked on (default `time`); people are checked only on that preview frame.

gap_radius.description: Comp pixels: gaps narrower than ~2× this between kept pieces are reported (default 100; raise to 150–200 to catch wider holes).

preview_dir.description: Absolute folder for the preview PNGs (default: the system temp folder, files overwritten each call). Use the chat's working folder.

tool_code.description: Project.toolType code of the Object Matte tool (default "161", AE 26.5). The tool reads the active tool and presses Option+W only until this code is active — Option+W is the Roto Brush group's shortcut and cycles its members.

dry_run.description: Find the picture and report the mapping without clicking.

shot_path.description: Absolute path to save the capture with the picture rectangle (PNG, ≤ 1600 px wide) for the user.
